universalAnswers.whatHappened: Microsoft opened a six-week consultation on a first draft AI behavior code September 14.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: A model is the trained component producing outputs; MAI denotes Microsoft AI-developed models.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: Official announcement and complete draft captured September 15 support the invitation, intended rules and limits.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: Written objectives are not present performance evidence or complete deployment safeguards.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: Readers can contribute a concrete concern before future guidance is revised.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: General public, Users and Operators, researchers, governments and Microsoft AI training teams are named audiences.
universalAnswers.changesNow: The consultation is open; the draft is not used for training today and no current account change is announced.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Final wording and which feedback is incorporated remain undecided.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Read one relevant passage and describe a stopping situation using the official linked form.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: What would a safe stop mean in a situation I know?

legal-policy.legalStatus: A voluntary provider draft consultation, not legislation, a court judgment or an enacted product requirement.
legal-policy.jurisdiction: Scope is Microsoft AI-developed MAI models, not models merely hosted or used by Microsoft.
legal-policy.parties: Microsoft AI authors and revises; public respondents can offer views without guaranteed incorporation.
legal-policy.allegationVsFinding: Microsoft states intended future behavior; the draft expressly acknowledges a gap from actual model behavior.
legal-policy.currentEffect: Public feedback can be submitted now; no present settings instruction is supported.
legal-policy.unresolvedQuestions: Revised text, implementation and measured adherence remain to be established.
legal-policy.nextMilestone: Consultation closes after six weeks; Microsoft plans a learned/changed summary and revised code later in 2026.

translation.newsVersionExact: Microsoft AI opened a six-week public consultation on September 14 about how its future MAI models should behave.
translation.actualMeaningExact: The draft Humanist AI Code of Conduct is not being used to train models today.
translation.mechanismExact: Publishing that rule makes the intention inspectable. It does not show that a model reliably follows it.
translation.familiarExampleExact: Imagine asking an AI to prepare a message, then cancelling.

jargon.plainMeaning: the trained component that produces AI outputs

learningConnections.learningPayoff: Understanding AI helps readers bring precise concerns to decisions about its future.
